A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RICH research work. All 17 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including their figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. The original experiments can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original PGD attack experiments, Attack-Bard classification results, and VLM-description-to-Claude experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds InternVL adversarial finetuning and reasoning experiments, together with prompt and prefill controls.

M1.justification: v1 primarily uses existing robust models with prompt repetition and CoT. v2 additionally constructs a robust InternVL 3.5 gpt-oss 20B through adversarial finetuning of its vision encoder and introduces budget-forced reasoning for this model. Section 4.4 and Appendix E establish a substantial new training and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Attack-Bard, visual prompt injection, and shape/color/texture classification remain the main evaluation coverage; Figure 7 identifies the four previously used images. New Table 1 lists COCO, Flickr30k, VQAv2, and TextVQA results, but their attribution and protocols do not establish whether these represent additional evaluations by this work or a summary of prior results.

E2.justification: Figures 1 and 8 add unmodified InternVL 3.5 gpt-oss 20B as the comparator for its adversarially finetuned variants. The original LLaVA, FARE, Delta2, Qwen, Llama, and frontier-model comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The original main-text protocols remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce prefill and token-content controls, an 8/255 attack budget, and budget-forced reasoning up to 64K tokens with 9,000- and 16,000-iteration finetuning checkpoints. InternVL Figure 1 uses the Attack-Bard label subset, whereas Figure 8 uses all 1,000 ImageNet classes. Tables 7 and 8 also use different sample coverage.

E4.justification: New Appendix B tests goal-only versus security specifications, prefill removal, and length-matched random prefills. Appendix C tests the less leading 'object' prompt and random versus meaningful added tokens. Appendix E examines finetuning checkpoints and long reasoning budgets, while Figure 1 adds a weevil reasoning case study. These substantially expand tests of mechanisms and sensitivity.

E5.justification: v1 already reports standard deviations, standard errors, and McNemar tests. v2 additionally specifies two replicates for Tables 7–8 and at least ten runs per configuration for Figure 8's standard errors. These are new reporting details for added experiments, not evidence that the original experiments received more runs.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 are numerically unchanged as v2 Tables 2–5. v2 adds InternVL accuracy curves, prefill and prompt-control results, and multi-benchmark robustness scores. The cited VQAv2 example changes from FARE 31% and Delta2 59.5% to 23.0 and 61.0 in new Table 1; insufficiently matched evaluation details prevent interpreting these as performance changes under the same conditions.

T1.justification: RICH remains a qualitative hypothesis. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no mathematical derivation or substantive formal definition. Reformatting the hypothesis and revising its conceptual discussion do not constitute theoretical changes.

C1.justification: The central RICH claim and recommendation to combine training and inference defenses remain. However, contribution 3 now claims creation of the first adversarially robust RL-tuned reasoning VLM, and the abstract foregrounds its robustness gains. This adds a substantial model contribution beyond v1's experiments with existing models; the earlier no-RL findings remain in the body.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly qualifies the specification benefit through meaningful prefill and proposes a termination-probability explanation; Appendix C argues that token meaning matters. Section 5 adds clean-performance costs and limits the training recommendation toward security applications. Figure 8 attributes uneven scaling possibly to degraded capabilities. v1's broader representation-based extension of RICH is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds a substantial training recipe: 16,000 iterations, the 9,000-iteration checkpoint, four H100 GPUs, batch size 12, two PGD steps, attack epsilon 4/255, step size 2/255, and clean-loss weight 0.5. It also identifies the system-message source and inherited defaults. Figure 7 documents all four existing white-box images; the original prompts are retained in Appendix D.

R1.justification: v2 adds the s1 budget-forcing and InternVL 3.5 references, removes the Goyal et al. VQAv2 reference, and adds the robust reasoning-VLM novelty claim. Its broader positioning relative to Zaremba and adversarial training remains stable. The Delta2 reference changing from Wang et al. 2025b to 2025c is only relabeling.

P1.justification: The abstract, methodology, reasoning-experiment discussion, limitations, and author contributions receive selective edits. The main five-section narrative and most existing prose remain intact. New analysis appendices move the original prompts from B to D and the color example from C to F, with corresponding reference updates.

P2.justification: v2 adds the first-page overview and reasoning plot, the prompt-injection comparison grid, an image gallery, and the long-budget plot, plus Tables 1 and 6–8. Retained tables are restyled and the RICH statement receives a new box. All five original figures remain, with changed placement and numbering.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked a directly robustified RL reasoning VLM and controls separating useful token content from token quantity. v2 adds both, substantially strengthening tests of its central hypothesis through Section 4.4 and Appendices B, C, and E. The training recipe and explicit prefill and clean-performance qualifications also improve reproducibility and interpretation. Uneven long-budget behavior and differing coverage in the token controls still limit universal or causal conclusions.
